1.explanation: The issue stems from how ModalComponent renders ReactModal without disabling overlay‐click or mousedown closure. By default, ReactModal will fire onRequestClose when a click (or drag) begins outside the modal content. The only relevant function in this file is ModalComponent, which directly renders ReactModal. To fix the bug, ModalComponent must pass props like shouldCloseOnOverlayClick={false} (or similar react-modal configuration) to prevent accidental closure when dragging outside the modal.
1.bug_scenario: In the sound‐recording modal, when the user clicks and drags the sound‐selection handles toward the edge of the modal, moving the mouse briefly outside the modal’s overlay causes the ReactModal component to treat it as an overlay click and automatically close the modal—discarding the user’s in-progress recording.

2.explanation: The entire modal UI is rendered by ModalComponent using ReactModal. By default, ReactModal will close when you click (or release the mouse) on its overlay. A drag that exits and re-enters the modal boundary can inadvertently fire that overlay click and trigger onRequestClose. To fix the bug you must modify ModalComponent (in src/components/modal/modal.jsx) – specifically the ReactModal instantiation – to disable or conditionally suppress overlay clicks (for example by adding shouldCloseOnOverlayClick=false or upgrading react-modal to a version with the drag-outside fix). This prevents unintended closures when dragging just outside the modal.
2.bug_scenario: When the user is dragging the sound waveform selection handle all the way to the right in the Record Sound modal, if the cursor briefly leaves the modal’s overlay/content region, ReactModal treats that “drag off” as a click on the overlay and invokes onRequestClose—closing the modal and losing all unsaved work.
